title: e2e webServer port 3111 shared with sibling repos; a stale serve_demo broke the fresh-clone verify
symptom: On a fresh clone, `python scripts/verify.py --e2e` failed at the e2e step: Playwright timed out 120s waiting for http://127.0.0.1:3111/client-portal/. A stale `serve_demo.py --port 3111 --base-path docs-answer` process left over from docs-answer's earlier verify was holding the port and serving a different base path, so the URL never came up.
reproduce: python scripts/serve_demo.py --port 3111 --base-path docs-answer &  # simulate a stale sibling server
python scripts/verify.py --e2e  # e2e step times out on the webServer URL
expected: Each repo's demo e2e binds a port no sibling uses; a leftover server from one repo cannot break another's verify.
regression_test: frontend/tests/e2e/core-journey.spec.ts asserts the origin port; playwright.config.ts port is now unique per repo (this repo: 3112).
root_cause: The scaffold template hardcoded port 3111 for every repo's serve_demo webServer, and rescue-scanner, client-portal and docs-answer all instantiated it unchanged. Playwright can leave a spawned webServer behind when a run is interrupted, so any stale sibling server occupying 3111 poisons this repo's e2e.
bench_note: Failure is environmental (a second process holding the port); not reproducible by a single bounded test inside this repo.
notes: Same fix applied in docs-answer (-> 3113); the scaffold template now assigns the next free port per new repo.
